content.text: The text combines Ovidian footnotes, a history of the French royal family’s imprisonment and executions, and a biography of astronomer Asaph Hall and his wife Angeline. It describes the royal family’s confinement in the Temple, Louis XVI’s trial and execution at the Place de la Révolution, Marie Antoinette’s removal to the Conciergerie and execution, the separation and death of the Dauphin, and Madame Royale’s release from the Temple and travels to Vienna, Mittau, England, and France. Angeline Stickney’s childhood in Rodman, schooling at McGrawville, teaching career, marriage to Hall, and movements through Ann Arbor, Shalersville, Cambridge, Washington, and Georgetown are traced. Her devotion supported Hall’s astronomical career, family, charitable work, scientific interests, and education of their four sons.
